text:
Sam (Sales): Quick Q from an enterprise prospect — they want CAIQ mapping for data residency and KMS responsibilities across our deployment modes. Also need POC evidence. Who owns what for Hosted / Dedicated / Private? @Maria (Security) @Jessica (Presales)

Maria (Security): TL;DR: Hosted = Redwood-managed KMS by default (we handle key lifecycle + HSM). Dedicated = customer can opt for BYOK/Tenant KMS on reserved pools (we support Bring Your Own Key + key policies). Private (VPC/on-prem) = customer-managed KMS and keys. For CAIQ, we'll map controls to our artifacts + call out customer responsibilities (network, tenant-level key custody, IAM).

Ali (Infra): Details: Hosted: envelope encryption w/ CMK backed by our KMS; rotation cadence 90 days; no tenant key separation unless customer requests BYOK. Dedicated: supports tenant keys via customer KMS or our KMS with key import; we provide steps + CLI snippets for key binding. Private: we ship connectors/integration points only — key storage and rotation are customer's responsibility.

Jessica (Presales): For the CAIQ and vendor-risk packet I'll assemble a mapping doc and attach evidence. Need to confirm: does the prospect require tenant-level BYOK for the POC, or is region-level ok? If BYOK, we need their KMS contact and whether HSM attestation is required.

Sam (Sales): They said BYOK for data in EU and auditor wants key custody proof. POC window starts next Monday. Can we hit 2 business days for initial CAIQ answers + evidence list?

Maria (Security): Yes, we can produce initial mappings in 48 hours. Evidence we can provide quickly: SOC2 summary, KMS architecture diagram, key policy example, encryption-at-rest statement, sample key rotation log, API call audit snippet. Items that require customer input: tenant KMS configs, external HSM attestations, network ACLs.

Ali (Infra): I'll export the key policy and rotation log. Example snippet for CAIQ control mapping (quick):
```
CCM-01: KMS managed by Redwood (Hosted) — Evidence: KMS-diagram.pdf, rotation-log-2026-03.csv
CCM-01b: Tenant BYOK (Dedicated) — Evidence: BYOK-integration-guide.md, key-binding-screenshot.png
CCM-02: Private deployments — Evidence: onprem-key-instruction.doc, customer-signed-key-responsibility.pdf
```

Jessica (Presales): Action items:
- Jessica: draft CAIQ responses + evidence bundle (EOD Tue)
- Ali: export key rotation logs + key policy scrns (tomorrow)
- Maria: review CAIQ mappings and call out control exceptions (48h)
- Sam: share prospect KMS contact and regulatory requirements (today)

Sam (Sales): Shared. Prospects' auditor also asked about log retention and egress controls. They require proof that customer data never leaves EU region unless explicitly configured.

Maria (Security): We have region routing policy and egress controls; will include a network flow diagram and the egress policy snippet. Also note: our default hosted backups are region-local; cross-region replication is opt-in and documented.

Jessica (Presales): OK — will include a short SOW blurb for POC: "Data will remain in EU region; BYOK will be integrated for tenant key custody; Redwood provides KMS integration support and attestation artifacts during POC." I'll post draft here when ready. :thumbsup:

Ali (Infra): FYI posting CLI command for binding a customer key to a dedicated pool (useful for POC):
```
redwood-cli kms bind --pool-id <pool> --key-arn <customer-key-arn> --region eu-west-1
```

Maria (Security): Looks good. Once Jessica posts the draft I'll give a final stamp. If auditor wants HSM attestation, we'll need customer's HSM vendor certs or we can provide our HSM supplier attestation for hosted keys.

Sam (Sales): Thanks team. Jessica — can you ping when draft is up? I'll coordinate with prospect. :eyes:

Jessica (Presales): Will do. Plan: post CAIQ draft + evidence checklist by 2026-03-24 17:00 CET. Adding action items to the POC workspace. /cc @Sam (Sales) @Maria (Security) @Ali (Infra)

Maria (Security): :thumbsup: done.

(End of thread)
